findings.reason: The original standalone tiles show only text and formulas for a concrete geometric rotation. A profile and projected circular sections materially clarify the positive interior radius, the axis, angular parameter and endpoint collapse; the complete proof does not remove this explanatory benefit. The local surface-integral supplier explicitly parametrizes exactly this surface.
findings.action: Added a fenced TikZ profile and projected wireframe, with precise parametrization and projection caption, at the end of Remarks.

correction: Added an explanatory sine profile and surface-of-revolution diagram in Remarks; all prior source text and complete frontmatter are preserved.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Profile r(x)=sin x on [0,pi]; surface Phi(x,theta)=(x,sin x cos theta,sin x sin theta) on [0,pi] x [0,2pi].
diagram_math_checks.justification: The Example and Given specify this rotation; thm-scalar-surface-integrals-on-a-surface-of-revolution Statement supplies exactly this parametrization with s=x and r=sin x.

diagram_math_checks.relation: At each fixed x, the circular section has radius sin x; r>0 in the interior and r=0 at both endpoints.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Existing facts L1 and L2 establish positivity and endpoint zeros. Thus both endpoint circles collapse to points. The source supplier proof step 2.1 treats precisely these allowed boundary collapses.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Right panel projects (X,Y,Z) to (X+0.35Z,Y+0.22Z). Five complete sections at x=k*pi/6 (k=1,...,5) therefore project to (x+0.35r sin theta,r cos theta+0.22r sin theta).
diagram_math_checks.justification: Substitution in Phi proves the plotted relations. An actual numeric check of all 61 samples in each of five sections found max coordinate rounding error 0.0000495481 and exact equality of each sampled first/last point. The actual compiled native image shows five closed ellipses.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The two blue meridians are theta=0 and theta=pi, namely (x,+/-sin x) in the specified projection. The marked angular sector lies at x=pi/2, from theta=0 to pi/3.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Substitution in Phi gives the meridians. The sector endpoint is (pi/2+0.35 sin(pi/3),cos(pi/3)+0.22 sin(pi/3)), rounded to (1.8739,0.6905); its inner arc uses the same projection with radial factor 0.47. Thus the caption correctly identifies a projected angle rather than an undistorted planar angle.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The area density remains sin x sqrt(1+cos^2 x), integrated over x and theta.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Supplier proof step 1.1 computes r sqrt(1+r′^2); local Verification 1.1 substitutes r=sin x. Independently, u=cos x changes the integral to integral from -1 to 1 of sqrt(1+u^2), equal to sqrt(2)+arsinh(1), preserving the displayed area. The existing rigorous argument remains verbatim and independent of the figure.
